title: Convergent Detour Hijacking: The Attack That Lets Your Agent Succeed
hook: A malicious third-party skill doesn't have to break your agent's task. It can just take the scenic route — burning 67% more tokens and 92% more wall-clock while the final answer still looks correct.
key_points: Skill-based agents expose two control points to untrusted publishers: the skill description (used for selection) and the instruction body (used for planning).
Convergent Detour Hijacking (CDH) is a text-only, runtime-independent attack that chains both stages under shared semantic cover.
The description wins selection; the aligned body then fabricates plausible dependencies that recruit extra benign skills into a bounded detour.
The detour re-enters the original route, so the task still completes — hiding the attack from outcome-based checks.
On DeepSeek-V4-Pro across 491 held-out tasks, the attacker's coordinator was selected in 80.02% of tasks.
Coordinator-hit runs that completed used 66.91% more tokens and 92.45% more end-to-end time, with comparable task completion.
content_html: Agents increasingly install third-party "skills": a natural-language description tells the agent when the skill is relevant, and an instruction body tells it what to do. Junliang Liu and co-authors (arXiv, August 2026) point out that this progressive-disclosure design hands an untrusted publisher two sequential control points — selection and planning — and show what happens when you attack both at once.
extra_html:
The attack

Convergent Detour Hijacking (CDH) is text-only and runtime-independent: no exploit, no privileged access, just carefully written skill text. Under shared semantic cover, the description establishes relevance so the attacker's coordinator skill gets picked alongside legitimate ones; the body then reuses that same rationale to fabricate plausible dependencies, pulling extra benign skills into a bounded detour before rejoining the original route.

Across 491 held-out tasks and multiple LLM backends, in single-task and multi-turn settings: on DeepSeek-V4-Pro the matched coordinator was selected in 80.02% of tasks, and among coordinator-hit runs that completed, token consumption rose 66.91% and end-to-end time 92.45% — while aggregate task completion stayed comparable.

Why it matters

Most agent evaluation asks "did it get the right answer?" This paper is a clean demonstration that the answer can be right while the trajectory is compromised. If your only guardrail is outcome quality, an attacker can quietly bill you for the difference.

related.title: Token Budgets: When Agents Burn Money
related.hook: A single retry loop can spend thousands of dollars before anyone notices. This paper catalogs 63 real budget-overrun incidents — and asks the type system to make over-spending a compile error.

related.title: Claude Agent Skills
related.hook: Agent Skills package instructions, scripts, and resources into folders an agent loads on demand — composable, portable expertise, later opened as a standard like MCP.

related.title: The Regression Tax on Agent Skills
related.hook: Handing an agent a procedural skill doesn't only add wins — it also breaks tasks it used to solve. The best skills win by regressing less, not by gaining more.

flashcards.prompt: What makes Convergent Detour Hijacking hard to catch?

choices.text: The detour returns to the original route, so the task still completes correctly
It requires privileged access to the agent runtime
It only triggers on inputs the defender cannot observe

flashcards.explanation_html: CDH preserves the outcome — aggregate task completion stays comparable — so anything checking only final answers sees nothing wrong. The damage is in cost and trajectory.

flashcards.prompt: Which two control points does a third-party skill expose to its publisher?
flashcards.back_html: The natural-language description, which decides whether the skill gets selected, and the instruction body, which shapes the agent's plan once selected.

flashcards.prompt: What does the paper conclude about outcome-based evaluation of agents?
flashcards.back_html: Correct outcomes do not guarantee trajectory integrity or cost safety — an agent can be steered onto an expensive detour and still finish the job.
